about: Objects in RJ's photo, with distances and sources. Built by scripts/catalog/build_objects.py; see data/SOURCES.md. Distances are in parsecs (1 pc = 3.2616 ly); lo/hi are the 1-sigma range. Positions are ICRS degrees at epoch 2026.71.

objects.name: Alcyone
objects.note: A member of the Pleiades, so it takes the cluster's distance, which is far better measured than any one star's.

objects.name: Almaaz
objects.note: Poorly measured: the parallax is 1.53 ± 1.29 mas.

objects.name: Alnilam
objects.note: The median distance of its association, Orion OB1b, from Gaia DR3 parallaxes of its fainter members. Hipparcos measured 606 pc, which is often quoted but unreliable for such a bright star.

objects.name: Alnitak
objects.note: The distance of its association, Orion OB1b, from Gaia DR3 parallaxes of its fainter members. The paper gives no uncertainty; ±8 pc is the one the same method gives for Alnilam. Hipparcos measured 226 pc.

objects.name: Orion Nebula
objects.note: Gaia DR2 parallaxes of 378 member stars. Radio (VLBA) parallaxes give 388 ± 5 pc (Kounkel et al. 2017) and 414 ± 7 pc (Menten et al. 2007).

objects.name: De Mairan's Nebula
objects.note: Part of the same cloud as the Orion Nebula, so it takes the Orion Nebula Cluster's distance. Gaia DR2 parallaxes of 378 member stars. Radio (VLBA) parallaxes give 388 ± 5 pc (Kounkel et al. 2017) and 414 ± 7 pc (Menten et al. 2007).

objects.name: M78
objects.note: Distance of NGC 2068, the young cluster whose light it reflects.

objects.name: Crab Nebula
objects.note: The remains of the supernova seen from Earth in 1054. Too faint to show in this photo. Radio parallax of the pulsar at its centre, 0.53 ± 0.06 mas. Gaia DR3's parallax of the pulsar agrees.

objects.name: λ Orionis Cluster
objects.mag_note: No integrated magnitude in OpenNGC; the card shows the brightest member instead.
objects.note: The cluster around Meissa, Orion's head.

objects.name: IC 348
objects.mag_note: No integrated magnitude in OpenNGC; the card shows the brightest member instead.
objects.note: A cluster still inside the Perseus molecular cloud, a few million years old.

objects.name: Orion's Belt
objects.note: Three unrelated-looking stars that really are neighbours: all three belong to the Orion OB1b association, about 1,250 light-years away.
